html:
SMTO-EML-0028 — Your email provider rejected the sign-in for this sender

GUID: e590c609-2c70-53b5-a0a5-7218612f085b
Slug: email-smtp-credentials-rejected
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • The mail server said the username and password, or sign-in approval, saved for this sender isn't accepted. No email was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open More options › Parameter Store, select the sender, open Value and select Reveal & edit value. Check that the username and password are current, then select Save. The server rejected exactly these saved sign-in details.
  2. If your provider requires an app password (for example Gmail with 2-Step Verification), create one in your email account and save it as the password. Many providers refuse your normal password when a program sends mail for you.
  3. If the sender signs in through your provider's approval screen (OAuth), ask SMTO in a conversation to connect the email account again. Reconnecting gets a fresh approval from your provider.
  4. Ask your email administrator whether sending mail by SMTP sign-in is allowed for your account, then ask SMTO to test the connection. Some organizations turn this off, and the server then rejects every sign-in.

What success looks like

  • The connection test reports success, showing that the sign-in worked.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to your email administrator or the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep trying password guesses; repeated failed sign-ins can get the account locked by your provider.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • SMTP AUTH returned reply 535 (credentials rejected, RFC 4954); the failure occurred before MAIL FROM, so no message was transmitted.

What this means

  • The SMTP server rejected the authentication exchange with reply 535. Classification uses the SMTP reply or negotiated capability, never the server response prose.

Why this can happen

  • The SMTP AUTH exchange returns the structured reply 535.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained operation, condition and effect evidence before choosing a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Check the profile's auth.username and password, or for OAuth the connection's token and granted scopes, and the mailbox's SMTP AUTH policy with the provider. Correct the credential or rerun email.connect, then email.test_connection; OAuth senders already received one automatic token refresh before this result.
  • Review the selected account credentials and allowed SMTP authentication policy; correct or reconnect the account through its supported authorization flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first; existing effect evidence and replay checks still decide whether a new attempt is permitted.

How to verify the fix

  • The reported prerequisite is satisfied and a new authorized operation returns its actual result.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a write whose external effect is still unknown.

Technical notes

  • Diagnostic presentation does not start recovery or alter authorization.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
